epigraphs.text: The forms of liberty may remain, while the spirit is gone.
Constitutions are chains of paper; power tests how easily they tear.
The first week of a regime tells you not what it has done, but what it intends to make normal.

long_synopsis: Trump’s second term begins with a deliberate shock to the architecture of American democracy. In five days, the presidency declares overlapping border and energy emergencies, attempts to narrow birthright citizenship by decree, suspends asylum and refugee programs, and militarizes immigration enforcement. Schedule F is revived, inspectors general are purged, and a new Department of Government Efficiency embeds Musk-led teams across agencies, politicizing and partially privatizing the civil service. Law is openly repurposed: more than 1,500 January 6 defendants and anti-abortion offenders receive clemency, Foreign Corrupt Practices Act enforcement is paused, and DOJ civil-rights and police-reform work is frozen, while sanctuary officials and prior leaders face investigation. Citizenship and belonging are redefined through English-only rules, gender and DEI rollbacks, and mass-deportation plans. Simultaneously, Trump launches personal cryptocurrencies, a sovereign wealth fund, and a bitcoin reserve, fusing public policy with private enrichment. Courts, states, unions, and civil-society groups respond with lawsuits and countervailing policies, but on a slower, reactive timeline. The Democracy Clock moves from 7:31 p.m. to 7:39 p.m., registering a sharp deepening of erosion rather than a single coup.
